worked_example.problem: The computer inside a cash machine (ATM) only lets people take out money and check their balance. How is it classified by purpose?
steps: It does only one kind of job.
A computer built for one job is special-purpose.

cards.idea: By size: supercomputers, mainframes, minicomputers, microcomputers (personal computers).
example: Your phone is a microcomputer; a weather service may use a supercomputer.

cards.idea: By data: analog, digital or hybrid. Most computers today are digital.
example: A digital computer works with numbers.

cards.idea: By purpose: general-purpose (many jobs) or special-purpose (one job).
example: A laptop is general-purpose; a washing machine’s computer is special-purpose.

right.text: the computer in a washing machine

wrong.explain: A laptop can do many jobs: general-purpose.

pick.t: the most powerful, used for weather forecasts
pick.why: Supercomputer: the most powerful, used for weather forecasts.

pick.t: serves thousands of bank customers at once
pick.why: Mainframe: serves thousands of bank customers at once.

pick.t: a laptop, desktop, tablet or smartphone
pick.why: Microcomputer: a laptop, desktop, tablet or smartphone.

questions.prompt: Which kind of computer is this: {x.t}?

misconceptions.explain: Not that kind. Think about size and power.

pick.t: measures quantities that change smoothly, like an old needle speedometer
pick.why: Analog: measures quantities that change smoothly, like an old needle speedometer.
Hybrid: can work in both ways.

misconceptions.explain: Digital: numbers. Analog: smooth measurements. Hybrid: both.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

wrong.text: A mainframe can serve only one user.
wrong.explain: A mainframe serves many users at once.

wrong.text: A washing machine’s computer is general-purpose.
